versions.title: FAQ: separate 'binding laws' from 'binding mechanisms'

changes.from: Eight binding instruments in this map carry penalty regimes: the EU AI Act (up to €35M or 7% of global revenue), China's GenAI Measures, Korea's AI Basic Act (~$21k per violation), California SB 53 (up to $1M per violation), the Colorado AI Act, the NY RAISE Act ($1M/$3M), Texas TRAIGA, and US BIS export controls. Most are phasing in; several face active federal preemption challenges in the United States.
changes.to: Five AI laws in this map are classed as binding with penalties: the EU AI Act (up to €35M or 7% of global revenue), China's GenAI Measures, Korea's AI Basic Act (~$21k per violation), California SB 53 (up to $1M per violation) and the NY RAISE Act ($1M/$3M). The map's wider 'binding with penalties' count also includes US BIS export controls and five regulators enforcing binding law (the EU AI Office, UK Ofcom, the UK ICO, Australia's eSafety Commissioner and the Colorado Division of Insurance). The Colorado AI Act and Texas TRAIGA are binding statutes the map classes as hard law with weak enforcement. Several US state laws face active federal preemption challenges.

evidence.supports: The FAQ list versus the pow values and stats tile

versions.uncertainty: Only the structure changes. The penalty figures (€35M/7%, ~$21k, $1M, $1M/$3M) and the 'phasing in' statement were not re-verified this run because their sources were blocked. I dropped 'Most are phasing in' rather than restate an unchecked status claim. If the EU Digital Omnibus lead is confirmed, the EU AI Act timing elsewhere will change, though not this sentence.

versions.title: Anthropic RSP: describe the v3 structure (thresholds, ASLs, safeguards, evaluations, timing) and the separate compliance framework

changes.from: Defines AI Safety Levels (ASLs) — currently up to ASL-3 — each tied to specific capability evaluations and mandatory safeguards: weight-security tiers, deployment mitigations, model-autonomy controls. The original published framework that set the template for the field; commitments include not deploying at a given ASL until the corresponding mitigations are in place. Subjected to detailed external scrutiny in EU GPAI Code drafting and California SB 53.
changes.to: Since v3.0 (Feb 2026) the policy separates Anthropic's own plans from more ambitious industry-wide recommendations, which Anthropic says it cannot commit to follow unilaterally. ASLs now label only the safeguards kept for current models (ASL-3). It adds a Frontier Safety Roadmap of public goals (not hard commitments) and Risk Reports every 3–6 months. The original published framework that set the template for the field. Anthropic's documents for California SB 53 and the EU GPAI Code are a separate Frontier Compliance Framework; the RSP remains its voluntary policy.

changes.from: AI Safety Levels (ASL-1, 2, 3, currently up to ASL-3) trigger graduated safeguards as capabilities cross specified evaluations. The original published framework that set the threshold-and-tier template; SB 53 codifies the underlying norm.
changes.to: Four capability thresholds (non-novel and novel chemical/biological weapons, misaligned AI in high-stakes settings, automated R&D), each mapped to Anthropic's planned mitigations and to recommended industry-wide mitigations. The original published framework that set the threshold-and-tier template; SB 53 codifies the underlying norm.

CAC Order No. 21 on humanlike interactive AI was issued 10 Apr 2026, in force 15 Jul 2026 (S-0056, S-0055). Removed as unsupported: 'Compute thresholds debated', 'competing proposals from MOST and CAIC' (no official source; 'CAIC' is unidentified), the draft-content claims in the coverage notes (no official draft exists), and 'near-term action looks unlikely' (the State Council's 2026 wording is 'accelerate'). The link is the NPCSC 2026 plan PDF, which settles the NPC status. 'Could consolidate…' softens a speculative claim. status 'proposed' and pow 2 are unchanged.

conflict_resolution.disagreement: The map, and trial-1 secondary leads, say the 2025 NPC plan dropped the AI law from preparatory items. The NPCSC 2025 plan lists 'healthy development of AI' legislation among its preparatory items.
conflict_resolution.explanation: The claims concern two different plans. The NPC Standing Committee kept AI legislation as a preparatory item in 2025 (S-0050; confirmed by the NPC committee report, S-0057). The State Council's plan named an 'AI Law draft' for preparatory submission in 2024 (S-0053) and replaced it with general wording in 2025 (S-0052). So 'dropped' is true of the State Council plan only. A trial-1 secondary claim of a second reading in Q4 2025 is not borne out: AI appears in neither the continued-review nor the first-review list of the NPCSC 2026 plan (S-0049).
